newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak Econ Ministry says NPF Nafta sale illegal.
newsitem.headline: Slovak Econ Ministry says NPF Nafta sale illegal.

text.p: The Slovak Economics Ministry on Wednesday said the state privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), violated the law when it sold off its holdings in oil and gas storage company Nafta.
"The NPF violated the law on strategic companies with the sale of its remaining shares in Nafta and not retaining a state interest in the company," Ministry Spokesman Jozef Sucha told Reuters.
NPF officials were not immediatelly available for comment.

The NPF raised eyebrows at the beginning of August when it sold its entire 45.9 percent stake in Nafta to the private, and little-known firm Druha Obchodna for 500 million crowns, far below its market value at the time of some 3.2 billion crowns.

An extraordinary shareholders' meeting, held on October 1 behind closed doors, approved new company statutes effectively cancelling the state's veto right over strategic decisions, including any changes to the company's basic capital.
Nafta is on a government list of strategic companies which should not have been privatised at all, or in which the government is to retain a "golden share" veto right over key decisions.

"The shareholders' meeting approved new statutes striking off a paragraph saying Nafta was a government listed strategic firm with capital participation of the NPF," a shareholder, who requested anonymity, said.
It was not immediately clear whether the new statutes had the legal power to annul the state's veto right over strategic decisions in Nafta.
